paragraphs: This paper studies how to find good values of a function whose possible inputs are the nodes of a graph. Ordinary graph search can explore this space, but may spend evaluations inefficiently and fail to exploit information from function values already observed. The authors bring Bayesian optimisation to this setting to make the search more informed.

Their framework learns suitable graph kernels: mathematical descriptions of relationships between nodes that help model the target function. Learning these relationships lets the search adapt to how the function behaves, rather than relying only on the graph's fixed structure. The method also uses local modelling to keep optimisation efficient on large graphs, including settings where the graph may initially be unknown.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world graphs demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The contribution combines adaptation to observed function values with an approach designed for computational efficiency. This matters because searching a graph involves both deciding where to evaluate next and keeping the model that guides those decisions manageable.
neurips-2023-bayesian-optimisation-of-fu.tldr: A Bayesian optimisation framework learns relationships between graph nodes and uses local models to search large, potentially unknown graphs efficiently.

paragraphs: Image moderation systems can be challenged by deliberate visual changes that hide problematic content from a model while preserving its intended meaning. This paper introduces an ImageNet-based benchmark for studying such obfuscations. Examples motivating the work include overlaying an image with benign pictures or patterns to interfere with automated recognition.

The benchmark considers substantial, adversarial changes to images. Its focus differs from attacks restricted to small changes under a mathematical distance measure: the intended content can remain present even when the picture changes dramatically. The authors also position these transformations beyond the corruption types covered by ImageNet-C and ImageNet-C-bar, aiming to capture a threat relevant to content filtering.

The study evaluates 33 pretrained models and trains additional models using different augmentations, architectures, and training methods on subsets of the obfuscations. This design examines whether exposure to some transformations helps with others. The stated contribution is a benchmark and evaluation programme that can support research into robustness against these deliberate alterations.
neurips-2023-benchmarking-robustness-to-.tldr: An ImageNet-based benchmark tests whether image models withstand drastic, deliberate obfuscations that preserve the original content's intent.

paragraphs: Masked image modelling trains a visual model by asking it to reconstruct missing image content, but the resulting representations can still be vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper investigates whether a related self-supervised task can contribute more directly to defence. The authors study noisy image modelling, which learns to reconstruct images after noise has been added.

They observe that this denoising task produces strong reconstruction even under severe corruption. Their defence, called De^3, uses the pretrained decoder's denoising capability to improve downstream classifiers' adversarial robustness. The decoder therefore contributes to defence alongside the features learned during pretraining. A further modification samples the noise-scale setting from random distributions, allowing adjustment of the balance between accuracy and robustness.

In the reported experiments, noisy image modelling provides stronger adversarial robustness than masked image modelling because of its denoising ability. Its defence performs on par with adversarial training while offering the additional tuning flexibility. These findings support using reconstruction capabilities learned during pretraining as an active component of a defensive system.
neurips-2023-beyond-pretrained-features-.tldr: A pretrained image-denoising decoder provides an adversarial defence with experimentally competitive robustness and an adjustable accuracy–robustness trade-off.

paragraphs: A neural network can perform a complex task well without making clear how it solves that task. This paper asks whether networks internally divide problems into reusable subroutines and combine their results. The authors call this structural compositionality, contrasting it with the possibility that a model mainly matches new inputs to learned templates.

To investigate, they use model pruning across vision and language, examining different architectures, tasks, and pretraining arrangements. Pruning provides a way to probe which parts of a network support particular functions. The central question is whether a subroutine has a sufficiently distinct internal implementation that it can be removed while other subroutines continue to work.

The results show that models often contain modular subnetworks with this property. Removing one can disrupt its associated subroutine while preserving the functionality of others. This offers evidence that neural networks can learn task decomposition internally. It also suggests that specialised symbolic mechanisms may not always be needed to obtain compositional behaviour, without establishing that every network learns it.
neurips-2023-break-it-down-evidence-for-.tldr: Pruning experiments find that neural networks often implement task subroutines in separable subnetworks, providing evidence for learned structural compositionality.

paragraphs: Tracking an object can require maintaining several plausible explanations of its hidden state. Particle filters represent these possibilities with weighted samples, but traditionally depend on specified models of motion and observations. This paper instead learns particle-based uncertainty representations from training data, using neural encoders to condition them on observations such as images.

The main technical challenge is training through the operations that maintain the particles. Earlier discriminative filters used approximate resampling rules or stopped gradients at resampling steps. The proposed method represents the posterior as a continuous mixture density and obtains unbiased, low-variance gradient estimates. The authors identify serious failures in existing reparameterisation-based mixture-gradient estimators and address them with an importance-sampling estimator.

The resulting mixture density particle filter explicitly preserves multiple possible continuous states. Across the studied tracking and robot-localisation problems, the authors report large accuracy improvements, greater robustness, and much more stable results across training runs. The work links those practical benefits to both the uncertainty representation and a more reliable way of learning it.
neurips-2023-differentiable-and-stable-l.tldr: A learned particle filter uses continuous mixture densities and importance-sampling gradients to improve multimodal tracking accuracy and training stability.

paragraphs: This paper studies causal relationships among variables that are themselves functions, such as signals varying over time. Its model allows the causal graph to contain directed cycles, so the structure need not follow a one-way ordering. The authors introduce a functional linear structural equation model to learn these relationships from multivariate functional data.

To make the structure easier to interpret, the model uses a lower-dimensional causal representation. Within the proposed formulation, this smaller space preserves the relevant causal information in the original functions. The authors prove causal identifiability under standard assumptions used in causal discovery. That qualification matters: the result establishes when the model's causal structure can be distinguished, rather than promising causal recovery from arbitrary observations.

Inference uses a fully Bayesian framework, with prior specifications and posterior summaries that quantify uncertainty. Simulation studies report better causal graph estimation than existing methods, and an EEG dataset provides an application. Together, the contributions combine cyclic causal modelling, a compact interpretable representation, and uncertainty-aware estimation.
neurips-2023-directed-cyclic-graph-for-c.tldr: A Bayesian model learns potentially cyclic causal relationships among functional variables, with identifiability under stated assumptions and posterior uncertainty estimates.

paragraphs: Self-supervised image learning often builds useful representations by associating different parts of an image. This paper investigates what happens when those associations become specific to individual training examples. The authors call this déjà vu memorisation: a model retains image-specific information instead of learning only broadly meaningful relationships between visual content.

Their central demonstration starts with a trained model and a background-only crop from one of its training images. Even though the crop contains material such as sky, grass, or water, the model can make it possible to infer the missing foreground object with high accuracy, or even reconstruct it visually. This reveals information about the training image beyond the content directly visible in the crop.

The study finds this behaviour across different self-supervised algorithms and shows that some design choices make it worse. Conventional representation-quality evaluations fail to detect it. The findings therefore identify a privacy risk that useful downstream representations can conceal, while also suggesting potential practical mitigation strategies rather than establishing that the risk has been eliminated.
neurips-2023-do-ssl-models-have-deja-vu-.tldr: Self-supervised image models can memorise training-specific associations that reveal foreground objects from background crops, escaping conventional representation-quality checks.

paragraphs: Giving a language model access to more context does not automatically make that context useful. When attention can consult many documents, relevant entries become rarer among irrelevant ones. This paper identifies a distraction problem: attention keys associated with different meanings can overlap, making useful information difficult for the model to distinguish.

Focused Transformer addresses this through a training process inspired by contrastive learning. It improves the organisation of the key–value space that attention uses to access information. The purpose is to help the model separate relevant entries from competing ones as the available context grows. The method can fine-tune existing large models, making context extension possible without requiring an entirely new model.

The authors fine-tune 3-billion- and 7-billion-parameter OpenLLaMA checkpoints to produce LongLLaMA models. They report improvements on tasks requiring long context and demonstrate passkey retrieval with a context length of 256,000. That demonstration establishes a specific long-context retrieval capability; the broader contribution is a training method aimed at making expanded attention memory more usable.
neurips-2023-focused-transformer-contras.tldr: Focused Transformer uses contrastive-inspired training to reduce attention distraction, enabling LongLLaMA models to retrieve passkeys from 256,000-length contexts.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a dataset and benchmarks for estimating lower-body movement from smart textile knee sleeves. The system connects wearable signals to human motion by collecting sleeve time-series data alongside synchronised motion-capture measurements. Those camera measurements provide reference labels for learning and evaluating the relationship between the wearable data and body pose.

The trained system generates three-dimensional human models using wearable data alone. Cameras therefore supply ground truth during data collection, while movement estimation itself can operate without them. The study covers different activities and reports extension to exercises and individuals not previously seen. It also examines joints beyond the knees, showing that the sensing arrangement supports a broader lower-body estimate.

The reported average error is 7.21 degrees across eight lower-body joints relative to the reference measurements. This supports the system's effectiveness in the evaluated movement settings. Because estimation relies on wearables, it avoids restrictions from camera occlusion and field of view. The authors identify potential uses in fitness, sport, healthcare, and rehabilitation.
neurips-2023-intelligent-knee-sleeves-a-.tldr: Smart textile knee sleeves estimate 3D lower-body motion without cameras at prediction time, reporting a 7.21-degree average error across eight joints.

paragraphs: A training loss tells a model what kinds of mistakes to correct, and useful guidance may change as learning progresses. Learning-to-teach methods let a teacher model adjust that loss for a student. This paper argues that existing teachers overlook two sources of information: their own previous experience and the evolving state of the loss function.

The proposed method treats loss adjustment as a task that unfolds over time. Memory units allow the teacher to use experience from earlier stages, rather than deciding only from the student's current condition. A Dynamic Loss Network also exposes information about the loss itself. Together, these changes give the teacher a richer basis for adapting the student's training objective.

Experiments show improved student learning and performance across various deep models on classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. The contribution is therefore a way to make training guidance depend on a continuing interaction between teacher, student, and loss. The reported improvements support the value of remembering how that interaction has developed.
neurips-2023-l2t-dln-learning-to-teach-w.tldr: L2T-DLN improves adaptive training losses by giving the teacher memory and information about the loss function's state.

paragraphs: Models can fit their training data exactly and still perform well on unseen examples. To understand this behaviour, researchers study simplified models whose generalisation can be calculated precisely. This paper examines deep models built from Gaussian random features, focusing on how structure in their weights changes the resulting learning curves.

Earlier analyses largely assumed independently and identically distributed Gaussian weights, allowing structure mainly in the input data. The authors relax that weight assumption and consider many layers of structured Gaussian features. They use the replica trick from statistical physics to derive learning curves, making it possible to examine how the location of weight correlations affects generalisation.

The results distinguish the first layer from later ones. Correlations between rows of the first feature layer can help generalisation, whereas structure in subsequent layers is generally harmful in the models studied. This shows that weight structure's effect depends on where it appears. The findings concern a tractable class of random-feature models and provide insight into that setting.
neurips-2023-learning-curves-for-deep-st.tldr: An analysis of deep Gaussian-feature models finds that first-layer weight correlations can help generalisation, while later-layer structure is generally detrimental.

paragraphs: Energy-based priors provide a flexible way to model the hidden variables used by generative models. Learning them requires samples from prior and posterior distributions, commonly obtained through Markov chain Monte Carlo, or MCMC. This paper targets a practical weakness: short sampling runs may not converge, producing poor samples that damage generation quality and destabilise training.

The problem is especially pronounced when a target distribution has many distinct high-probability regions or many dimensions. The authors introduce a diffusion-based method that learns to amortise long-run MCMC sampling, incorporating that method into a new training algorithm for latent-space energy-based models. The aim is to improve the sampling component on which learning depends.

The paper provides theoretical evidence that the learned amortisation is a valid long-run MCMC sampler. Experiments on several image-modelling benchmarks report better performance than strong comparison methods. These findings connect a sampling improvement to better generative modelling, treating the quality of prior and posterior samples as an important part of learning a useful latent distribution.
neurips-2023-learning-energy-based-prior.tldr: Diffusion-based amortisation of long-run MCMC improves sampling for energy-based latent priors, with theoretical support and stronger image-modelling results.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks learn solutions to partial differential equations by penalising violations of those equations during training. This paper asks whether they can also benefit from knowing the equation's symmetries. These Lie point symmetries describe transformations that preserve solutions, linking a learned solution to a family of nearby valid ones.

The authors introduce a symmetry loss alongside the usual equation-based training objective. It encodes the requirement that the symmetry group's infinitesimal generators preserve the equation's solutions. In plain terms, the network receives guidance about how a solution can change while remaining valid. This places information about relationships among solutions directly into the learning objective.

Empirical evaluations indicate that this additional inductive bias greatly improves sample efficiency. The result suggests that the network can make better use of training information when it learns both a solution and the neighbouring solutions generated by the equation's symmetries. The contribution is a loss-based route for bringing those mathematical relationships into physics-informed learning.
neurips-2023-lie-point-symmetry-and-phys.tldr: A loss that encodes PDE symmetries helps physics-informed neural networks learn related solutions and empirically improves sample efficiency.

paragraphs: Diffusion models benefit from mathematical expressions that make their noise processes and training objectives tractable. Those advantages become harder to retain when generated data must remain inside a constrained set. This paper introduces Mirror Diffusion Models to handle convex constraints while preserving the tractability that makes ordinary diffusion training practical.

The method uses a mirror map to construct a dual space that is an ordinary Euclidean space. It learns the diffusion process there, enabling constrained generation through this alternative representation. The authors derive efficient ways to compute mirror maps for common constraint sets, including simplices and Euclidean balls, and report substantially improved performance over existing methods.

The paper also explores using constraints to embed invisible, quantitative information in generated data as watermarks. Mirror Diffusion Models provide a way to generate within the sets used for that purpose. This is presented as a potential mechanism for safety and privacy applications, alongside the main contribution of retaining manageable diffusion learning on convex constrained domains.
neurips-2023-mirror-diffusion-models-for.tldr: Mirror Diffusion Models use a transformed Euclidean space to enable tractable generation under convex constraints, including explored watermarking applications.

paragraphs: A multiset is a collection in which order does not matter but repeated elements do. An injective representation assigns different outputs to different multisets, preserving their distinguishability. This paper closes a theoretical gap between representations built from polynomial moments and the neural-network-based moments used in practice.

The authors prove that neural moments can define injective multiset functions when the activation is analytic and non-polynomial. Their required number of moments is essentially optimal within a multiplicative factor of two. The proof introduces a finite witness theorem, which also supports new approximation results for functions on multisets and measures and new results about what graph neural networks can distinguish.

Two negative findings clarify the scope of this expressiveness. Moments from piecewise-linear networks cannot yield injective multiset functions. Moreover, even injective moment representations cannot be bi-Lipschitz, meaning they cannot preserve distances with uniform bounds in both directions. Thus, the paper establishes powerful distinguishability results while showing that exact distinction does not automatically provide uniformly stable distance preservation.
neurips-2023-neural-injective-functions-.tldr: Neural moments can distinguish multisets injectively with analytic non-polynomial activations, but piecewise-linear moments cannot, and distance preservation has fundamental limits.

paragraphs: Generalisation bounds aim to relate a model's properties to how well it performs beyond its training examples. This paper develops norm-based bounds for sparse ReLU networks, including convolutional networks. Its central idea is that the network's pattern of connections should enter the analysis, rather than being obscured by a less structured mathematical representation.

For convolutional layers, the authors use the norms of the filters themselves instead of the norms of the associated Toeplitz matrices. This lets the bounds account for sparse architectural structure more directly. They theoretically show that the resulting bounds are significantly tighter than standard norm-based bounds, offering a more informative estimate within this style of analysis.

On several simple classification problems, the bounds also give relatively tight empirical estimates of generalisation. Together, the theoretical and experimental results suggest that sparsity in both the target function and the model architecture helps explain deep learning's success. The empirical evidence is specifically about the simple classification settings evaluated, while the theoretical contribution concerns the improved bounds.
neurips-2023-norm-based-generalization-b.tldr: Generalisation bounds that account for sparse connections and convolutional filter norms are theoretically tighter and empirically informative on simple classification tasks.

paragraphs: Advertisers often control automated buying through settings such as budgets or return targets, while seeing little about the platform's underlying purchases. The outcomes can change with seasonality, market trends, or disruptions. This paper formulates the advertiser's problem as online learning: repeatedly choose those settings using limited feedback while respecting constraints over time.

The proposed primal-dual algorithm handles multiple decision variables, bandit feedback, and uncertain long-term constraints. Bandit feedback means the learner must work with the outcomes of its chosen actions rather than complete information about all alternatives. The primal-dual formulation combines the search for good decisions with the need to manage constraints across the sequence.

The authors establish low regret for several outcome-generating settings, including stochastic, adversarial, adversarially corrupted, periodic, and ergodic processes. The algorithm does not need to know which of these settings generated the observations. This adaptability is the main theoretical result, and the framework also applies to constrained online decision problems beyond advertising.
neurips-2023-online-ad-procurement-in-no.tldr: A constrained online-learning algorithm adapts advertising controls under limited feedback and achieves low regret across several unknown outcome-generating settings.

paragraphs: The Perception Test evaluates what pretrained multimodal models understand about events in videos. It organises evaluation around memory, abstraction, physics, and semantics, together with descriptive, explanatory, predictive, and counterfactual reasoning. This skill-oriented design aims to reveal abilities that broad task labels such as classification or tracking may not describe precisely.

The benchmark contains 11,600 real-world videos averaging 23 seconds, filmed by roughly 100 participants worldwide. Six kinds of annotation support both language and non-language evaluation, including questions and answers, object and point tracks, and timed action and sound segments. Evaluations probe transfer with no examples, a few examples, or limited fine-tuning across video, audio, and text.

The reported comparison finds a substantial performance gap between humans and leading video question-answering models: 91.4% versus 45.8%. This indicates considerable room for improvement on the benchmark's perceptual and reasoning demands. Public fine-tuning and validation data, together with a held-out test server, provide infrastructure for examining those capabilities consistently.
neurips-2023-perception-test-a-diagnosti.tldr: The Perception Test probes multimodal video understanding through explicit skills and reasoning types, revealing a large reported gap between models and humans.

paragraphs: This paper analyses when an overparameterised linear classifier generalises as its numbers of examples, features, and classes all increase. The analysis uses a specified Gaussian bi-level data model. Within that setting, the authors resolve a conjecture about which growth regimes lead to successful generalisation and which lead to failure.

Their tight bounds establish a sharp asymptotic distinction: the misclassification rate approaches either zero or one in the identified regimes. One consequence separates classification from regression. A minimum-norm classifier that fits the training data can be asymptotically worse than classifiers that do not interpolate, even in a regime where the corresponding minimum-norm interpolating regressor is known to be optimal.

The proof develops a variant of the Hanson–Wright inequality suited to multiclass problems with sparse labels. The authors also apply the analysis to multi-label classification under the same bi-level ensemble. The findings give precise conclusions for this mathematical setting and show why conclusions about interpolation in regression need not carry directly into multiclass classification.
neurips-2023-precise-asymptotic-generali.tldr: Under a growing Gaussian bi-level model, tight bounds identify when multiclass linear classification succeeds or fails and expose limits of minimum-norm interpolation.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient tuning adapts a large pretrained model using relatively small trainable components. These components are often embedded inside the main network, tying their design and learning closely to its architecture. Res-Tuning introduces a formulation that separates the tuners from the backbone, aiming to make adaptation more flexible and efficient.

The authors provide theoretical and empirical evidence that popular tuning methods have equivalent counterparts in this separated formulation. That allows different tuning strategies to fit within one framework and makes combinations easier to design. They also introduce a memory-efficient variant whose sequence of tuners forms a bypass detached from the main branch, so gradients are propagated only through the tuners.

This detachment additionally permits a single backbone forward pass for multi-task inference. Experiments on discriminative and generative tasks report better efficacy and efficiency than existing alternatives. The contribution therefore concerns both how adaptation modules can be organised and how separating their computation can reduce the work involved in training and serving adapted models.
neurips-2023-res-tuning-a-flexible-and-e.tldr: Res-Tuning separates adaptation modules from the backbone, enabling flexible tuning combinations and a memory-efficient variant with shared backbone computation.

paragraphs: Finding an object from a person's intention requires connecting a goal to what objects can offer. Someone wanting to rest might look for a bed or sofa without naming either. This paper introduces RIO, a dataset for studying object detection driven by such intentions in varied, real-world scenes.

The dataset addresses restrictions in earlier work's intention descriptions and vocabulary of object functions. It expresses intentions as natural sentences and connects those descriptions to the surrounding scene. This lets the benchmark represent a broader range of possible uses for objects, with the desired object depending on both the request and its visual context.

RIO includes 40,214 images and 130,585 intention–object pairs, spanning diverse scenarios and object categories. The authors use it to evaluate existing models' ability to reason about suitable objects in open environments. The contribution is a richer evaluation resource for linking language about goals to visual object selection, rather than treating detection solely as matching an image region to a named category.
neurips-2023-rio-a-benchmark-for-reasoni.tldr: RIO benchmarks object detection from scene-relevant natural-language intentions using 40,214 images and 130,585 intention–object pairs.

paragraphs: Learning molecular representations requires capturing relationships in three-dimensional geometry. This paper identifies challenges in doing so efficiently, including costly representations, underused vector features, and difficulty combining different geometric properties. SaVeNet, the Scalable Vector Network, is designed to address these issues while accommodating a range of geometric requirements.

The framework aims to represent molecular geometry without relying on costly embeddings and is reported to scale effectively when direction noise is introduced. The authors analyse its efficiency and its invariance and equivariance properties. These properties concern how outputs should remain unchanged or transform consistently when the represented geometry is transformed, providing a mathematical basis for the representation's behaviour.

Experiments assess both efficiency and expressiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets. The authors report empirical efficiency advantages over existing methods and state-of-the-art performance across several molecular representation tasks. The contribution combines an efficient geometric framework with evidence that it retains the expressive capacity needed for the evaluated molecular learning problems.
neurips-2023-savenet-a-scalable-vector-n.tldr: SaVeNet combines efficient vector-based molecular representations with analysed geometric properties and strong empirical performance across molecular learning tasks.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether supervised pretraining can produce a transformer that learns to make decisions from interactions supplied in its context. The Decision-Pretrained Transformer learns to predict an optimal action from a query state and a collection of interactions drawn from diverse tasks. The study covers bandits and Markov decision processes.

Despite the simplicity of that objective, the trained model exhibits several reinforcement-learning behaviours. It explores when interacting online and behaves conservatively when working from offline data, without explicit training objectives for those behaviours. The authors also observe generalisation to new tasks beyond the pretraining distribution and adaptation to previously unknown task structure.

The theoretical analysis connects DPT to Bayesian posterior sampling, a sample-efficient reinforcement-learning algorithm. This connection yields regret guarantees for the resulting in-context decision procedure and establishes that it can learn faster than algorithms that generated its pretraining data. Together, the findings show how supervised prediction across varied tasks can support adaptive decision-making through context.
neurips-2023-supervised-pretraining-can-.tldr: Supervised action prediction trains a transformer that performs reinforcement learning in context, with empirical adaptive behaviours and theoretical links to posterior sampling.

paragraphs: Multimodal datasets often pair some types of information while leaving other combinations unavailable. A model might see images with text and text with audio, yet never receive images and audio together. LoReTTa addresses how to train a shared model that can use such missing combinations at inference time.

Its self-supervised pretraining framework combines causal and masked modelling with transitivity and commutativity. The central idea is to connect modalities through an intermediate modality: training on pairs A–B and B–C can support modelling the relationship between A and C. The authors show that a transformer trained this way can handle mixtures including the unseen A–C pair and the unseen A–B–C triplet.

Evaluation spans synthetic, medical, and reinforcement-learning datasets. Across those domains, the resulting multimodal transformer consistently outperforms strong GPT, BERT, and CLIP baselines on tasks involving missing modality combinations. These findings support learning across partially connected datasets as a way to build models that remain useful when deployment requires combinations absent from pretraining.
neurips-2023-training-transitive-and-com.tldr: LoReTTa links partially paired modalities during pretraining so a transformer can handle modality combinations it never encountered together.

paragraphs: Robustness certification seeks mathematical guarantees that a model's predictions resist specified input changes. This paper studies how to scale deterministic certification based on Lipschitz bounds to larger and deeper networks. A central obstacle is that fast bounds for conventional residual blocks can be too loose to support effective certification.

The authors address the architectural issue with a new residual block that produces the Linear ResNet, or LiResNet. They also introduce Efficient Margin Maximization, called EMMA, as a training loss. It penalises worst-case adversarial examples from multiple classes simultaneously, stabilising robust training. The architecture and loss therefore tackle complementary problems in obtaining useful guarantees at scale.

Together, the methods achieve reported state-of-the-art robust accuracy on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet under perturbations measured by the Euclidean norm. The authors also report the first scaling of fast deterministic robustness guarantees to ImageNet. The result expands the size of problems reachable by this certification approach, with guarantees tied to the perturbation setting being considered.
neurips-2023-unlocking-deterministic-rob.tldr: LiResNet residual blocks and the EMMA loss enable stronger certified robustness and scale fast deterministic guarantees to ImageNet.
